headline: Executive order places reciprocal tariffs on imported goods to address long-running US trade deficits in goods.
what_it_does: This order sets a tariff, which is a tax on imports, on goods brought into the United States. The title calls it reciprocal, meaning it is tied to how other countries treat US goods. Its stated goal is to shrink the large yearly gap between what the US imports and what it exports. No summary was provided, so specific tariff rates, covered countries, and exceptions are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: They may owe new tariffs on products they bring in from other countries.
Prices on some imported goods may change if businesses pass tariff costs on to customers.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign countries and companies that sell goods to the US
who_it_affects.how: Their products may face new tariffs when entering the US market.
They could be affected if other countries respond to the tariffs or change their own trade rules.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed April 2, 2025; exact start dates for the tariffs are not given in the provided material.
